short: An 1879 supernatural tale by Ambrose Bierce.
note: A supernatural tale by Ambrose Bierce, first published in 1879 and collected in Can Such Things Be? (1893).

sources.label: Library of America · A Psychological Shipwreck

short: Fyodor Dostoevsky, author of Notes from Underground.
note: Fyodor Dostoevsky (1821–1881), Russian novelist. Notes from Underground (1864) is presented as the confessions and recollections of an isolated, argumentative former official.

short: A collection by Isak Dinesen, the pen name of Karen Blixen.
note: Seven Gothic Tales, a collection by the Danish writer Karen Blixen under her pen name Isak Dinesen, combining Gothic mystery with psychologically intricate narration.

sources.label: Penguin Random House · Seven Gothic Tales

short: A collection of poems by G. K. Chesterton.
note: The Wild Knight and Other Poems, a poetry collection by G. K. Chesterton, including a dramatic poem of the same name.

sources.label: G. K. Chesterton · The Wild Knight and Other Poems

short: A star system in Perseus with regularly recurring eclipses.
note: Beta Persei, traditionally called the Demon Star. Two of its stars orbit so that one periodically eclipses the other as seen from Earth, causing regular changes in brightness.

short: Gustave Doré, illustrator of the Bible.
note: Gustave Doré (1832–1883), French artist whose dramatic designs illustrated both the Old and New Testaments in a widely reproduced nineteenth-century Bible.

short: A small board used in attempted spirit writing.
note: A small board, traditionally mounted on wheels and fitted with a pencil, moved under the fingertips to produce supposedly automatic or spirit-guided writing.
Brown or tawny like a weasel’s summer coat; the adjective also means resembling or belonging to the weasel family.
Light-loving: used especially of plants that grow best with abundant light.

short: A neck ornament marking an officer’s rank.
note: Originally throat armor; later a crescent-shaped ornament worn at the neck as an officer’s badge of rank.
